item.title: College of West Anglia students visit Houghton Hall exhibition
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
College of West Anglia students visit Houghton Hall exhibition
Art and Design students from the College of West Anglia have visited Houghton Hall to study the work of British sculptor Lynn Chadwick. The Level 3 students viewed the artist’s distinctive figures as part of a project exploring the human form.
During the trip, the group made observations and sketches of the sculptures within the historic landscape. Course director Mark Mann said the experience helped students engage with new creative ideas, while student Lola Hammond described the visit as an inspiring opportunity to view the artwork in its setting. The project encourages students to consider how scale and materials influence the way sculpture is experienced.

item.description:

Campaign launched to improve child road safety in the Fens
A new road safety initiative, Be Bright Be Seen, is offering thousands of free reflective keyrings to schools, youth groups, and sports clubs across the region. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign aims to increase the visibility of children as the nights draw in and the clocks go back on Sunday, October 25.
Organisers are encouraging the use of reflective gear and bright clothing to help pedestrians and cyclists stand out to motorists. This follows recent national data showing a rise in road traffic injuries. Local teachers, coaches, and youth leaders can apply for an allocation of the free keyrings by visiting the Fenland Citizen website.

item.title: Appeal for volunteers and donations to support Feed Fenland
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Appeal for volunteers and donations to support Feed Fenland
The Wisbech-based charity Feed Fenland is calling for community support to maintain its meal service for vulnerable residents. The organisation provides hot evening meals six nights a week at The Olive Academy on Coalwharf Road, often serving up to 200 portions per night.
Operating without government or large-scale charity funding, the service relies entirely on donations and volunteers to cover costs, which average £80 per night. The charity is currently seeking more people to assist with cooking, serving, and general operations. Those interested in volunteering or providing financial support can contact the team via email at correspondence@feedfenland.com.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Dragon Festival returns next month
The King’s Lynn Dragon Festival is set to return on Saturday, November 7, offering a variety of free family activities across the town. Cultural and heritage venues will host performances, trails, and medieval-themed entertainment between 10am and 3pm.
Events include a dragon hunt, archery, and live shows at the Minster, alongside craft sessions at the local library. Several venues are participating, including the Lynn Museum, St George’s Guildhall, and True’s Yard. Free cinema screenings are also available at the Majestic and Corn Exchange, though tickets for these must be booked in advance. Residents are encouraged to check with individual venues, as some activities have limited capacity.

item.title: King’s Lynn mother urges residents to trust their instincts on health
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn mother urges residents to trust their instincts on health
A King’s Lynn mother is encouraging people to seek medical advice if they notice unusual changes in their health, even after receiving clear screening results. Emma Lambert, 49, was diagnosed with secondary breast cancer in 2024 after noticing discomfort, despite a recent clear mammogram. Following her diagnosis, she is supporting the ‘My Life, My Way’ campaign by the charity Make 2nds Count. The initiative aims to raise awareness of secondary breast cancer and highlight the importance of listening to your body. Ms. Lambert, who now focuses on local wellbeing activities, is sharing her story to ensure others understand the signs and know that support is available for those living with the condition.

item.title: Wisbech NHS Retirement Fellowship hosts harvest celebration
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech NHS Retirement Fellowship hosts harvest celebration
The Wisbech branch of the NHS Retirement Fellowship held its annual harvest festival meeting this Wednesday at St Joseph’s Hall. Twenty-one members attended the event, which featured a lunch of jacket potatoes and salads, followed by homemade desserts. The afternoon included a programme of harvest-themed songs, poetry readings, and a raffle.
The group also began preparations for their October meeting, where members will learn to make Christmas candles with beekeeper Fiona Henderson. The fellowship meets on the final Wednesday of every month at 1.30 pm at the hall on Queens Road. New members are welcome to attend.

Nominations open for 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
Nominations are now being accepted for the 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards. Businesses have until 5pm on Friday, November 27, to submit entries across 11 different categories, including the Best Established Business of the Year.
The awards ceremony, now in its 38th year, is scheduled for Friday, March 5, 2027, at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn. Judges will also select an overall Mayor’s Business of the Year from the category winners. Further details on how to enter are available through the event organisers.

item.title: Three sentenced following Wisbech assault and false imprisonment
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Three sentenced following Wisbech assault and false imprisonment
Three people have been sentenced at Peterborough Crown Court following an incident in Wisbech on March 17. Two women were held against their will at a property on Waterlees Road and subjected to physical assaults.
David Warden, 52, of Belt Drove in Elm, and 24-year-old Bricy Upton were each jailed for 30 months after admitting to two counts of false imprisonment. Warden was also sentenced for possession of heroin. Sharne Boon, 33, was ordered to complete 60 hours of unpaid work after admitting to two counts of assault. All three defendants have been issued with ten-year restraining orders, preventing them from contacting the victims.

item.description:

Fire crews tackle blaze in Elm
Firefighters from six stations were called to Nettle Bank in Elm yesterday afternoon following reports of a fire. Crews from Wisbech, March, Chatteris, Outwell, Thorney and Ramsey arrived at 4:33pm to find a large bonfire spreading towards a nearby building.
Wearing breathing apparatus, teams used hose reels and jets to extinguish the flames and prevent further damage. Firefighters remained on the scene until 9:15pm and have since conducted regular inspections to ensure the area is safe. Officials have confirmed the cause of the fire was accidental.

King’s Lynn man honoured for charity work in Indonesia
A King’s Lynn man has received national recognition for his efforts to support communities in Indonesia. Samuel Oakes was highly commended in the international impact category at the inaugural University of Worcester Alumni Awards.
Mr Oakes, an outdoor adventure leadership and management graduate, founded the UK-registered charity ATOVA International. His work focuses on education, youth development, and health. Mr Oakes, who has spent the last decade living alongside the communities he serves, described the award as a surreal moment after years of working away from home.

Fenland residents invited to share views on dog control rules
Fenland District Council is seeking public feedback on proposals to extend dog control regulations across the region. The current Public Spaces Protection Order, which mandates rules such as keeping dogs on leads in cemeteries and fenced play areas, is due to expire this December.
The consultation, which began on September 11, asks residents for their views on extending these measures for another three years until December 2029, alongside potential minor adjustments. You have until October 9 to submit your response. Feedback will be presented to cabinet members in November to help decide whether to extend, amend, or end the order. Full details are available on the Fenland District Council website.

Over 10,000 sign petition to support Queen Elizabeth Hospital
A campaign to protect vital services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has reached a significant milestone, with more than 10,000 people signing a petition. Liberal Democrat Rob Colwell, who is leading the initiative, thanked the public for their support in safeguarding local emergency and hospital care.
Supporters are now being invited to take part in a demonstration at the Tuesday Market Place on October 17. Participants are asked to gather at 11:30 am for a "Human A&E queue" event. Attendees are encouraged to bring a sign displaying their home town or village and their travel time to the hospital, as the QEH Community Action Group prepares to submit the petition.

Peterborough City Council updates flood risk policy for new builds
Peterborough City Council has announced new measures regarding flood risk management for upcoming property developments. The local authority is implementing updated guidelines to ensure that new construction projects across the area properly account for potential flooding. These changes are designed to address environmental safety standards for future housing and commercial sites within the city’s jurisdiction. Residents and developers are advised to consult the council’s official planning documentation for further details on how these updated requirements may affect new building applications moving forward.
